method: coarse_cluster_llm_merge (K-means + LLM merge, round 1 only, no round-2 consolidation)

modes.canonical_name: Declaring completion without successful required verification
modes.definition: The agent claims completion, readiness, or successful validation while one or more explicitly required checks are unexecuted, stale, pending, simulated, blocked without disclosure, or failing.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create a verification ledger from every explicit command, manual check, acceptance criterion, and required CI job; record a fresh post-edit invocation, terminal status, exit code, and required observable result for each entry, and block completion, commit, push, PR, handoff, or completion-signal claims unless every entry passed through the prescribed path or is explicitly reported as blocked and unverified.

modes.canonical_name: Ending with explicit requirements unfinished
modes.definition: The agent ends or claims completion while one or more explicit requested steps, deliverables, fixes, artifacts, or workflow actions remain uncompleted without an accepted blocker or deferral.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Maintain a persistent acceptance ledger populated from every user request and approved plan, map each item to required completion evidence such as a diff, command result, created artifact, remote action, or returned URL, and block session termination or completion claims until every item has verified evidence or an explicitly reported blocker or user-approved deferral.

modes.canonical_name: Modifying paths outside explicit authorization
modes.definition: The agent modifies, deletes, or commits a path outside the exhaustive set explicitly authorized by the user.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Derive an exact write-path allowlist from the latest instruction, enforce it across all mutating tools, and compare the final or staged diff against it so every out-of-scope path is blocked, reverted, or separately approved.

modes.canonical_name: Claiming complete scope without deliverable evidence
modes.definition: The agent claims all requested or approved work is complete even though required files, components, tests, documentation, workflow outputs, plan slices, or other deliverables are absent or unresolved.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Build a persistent scope ledger from the request, approved plan, and proposed completion summary; assign each item a required artifact path or falsifiable acceptance criterion, compare file-backed items with on-disk existence and the final diff, record execution evidence for behavioral items, and block full-completion claims until every entry has evidence or explicit user-approved deferral.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting an explicitly requested remote push
modes.definition: The agent commits requested changes locally but ends without pushing them to the intended remote branch.
modes.canonical_mitigation: For every request requiring remote publication, add a mandatory push step and compare the local HEAD with the intended remote or pull-request head before completion, reporting any push error instead of stopping silently.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting or substituting required deliverables
modes.definition: The agent claims completion while one or more explicitly required paths, symbols, functions, or content changes are absent or implemented in a substitute artifact.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Generate a manifest of every required created, modified, and deleted path plus each named symbol, function, or content criterion, and block completion unless the final diff satisfies every manifest entry at its assigned location without unexplained substitutes.

modes.canonical_name: Expanding or substituting the approved task scope
modes.definition: The agent changes behavior or code regions that do not map to the approved task, sometimes while leaving the requested behavior unimplemented.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create a task-to-diff trace listing the approved behaviors and code regions, require every proposed and final changed hunk to map to one listed item or a documented necessary dependency, and block or separately present unmatched hunks for explicit approval.

modes.canonical_name: Writing without implementation authorization
modes.definition: The agent mutates repository state while the current request authorizes only diagnosis, review, exploration, planning, or another read-only activity.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Classify each request as read-only or implementation-authorized, run read-only requests with all mutating tools disabled, and enable writes or commits only after recording explicit implementation approval; compare pre- and post-task state before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Prolonged tool use without user-facing progress
modes.definition: The agent exceeds a reasonable tool-call or elapsed-time budget without providing the requested answer, proposal, plan, findings, or an informative progress update.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Enforce a checkpoint after five tool calls or two minutes of elapsed work: the agent must report current findings and status and, when enough evidence exists, provide the requested answer, proposal, or plan before further tool use; a still-running command must receive another status update at each subsequent two-minute interval.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting requested pull-request publication
modes.definition: The agent completes or begins local repository work but stops without pushing the branch and creating the explicitly requested pull request.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Expand every pull-request request into required commit, branch-push, PR-creation, and PR-URL verification steps, and block completion until each has a successful result or a concrete blocker is reported.

modes.canonical_name: Parsing data against an unverified schema
modes.definition: The agent maps persisted, imported, or third-party data using assumed fields or compatibility rather than the producer's actual schema.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Capture representative real fixtures for every producer, derive mappings from those fixtures or the authoritative format specification, and require parser tests asserting all required fields and downstream outputs before integration.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving consumers on a retired behavior
modes.definition: The agent changes a shared behavior, option, API, or resolution mechanism without migrating every producer and consumer that depends on it.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before completion, build a repository-wide producer-and-consumer inventory using symbol, value, and call-graph searches; update every listed path and run focused tests for each workflow and language.

modes.canonical_name: Claiming broad verification after running an incomplete acceptance matrix
modes.definition: The agent claims a change is fully verified despite not executing every suite, target, mode, reproduction command, and quality gate required by the claimed scope.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Maintain a claim-to-verification matrix populated from changed components and explicit requirements, record the command and successful result for every applicable entry, and block completion claims until no required entry is missing or failing.

modes.canonical_name: Incomplete migration after tightening an input contract
modes.definition: The agent tightens a validated input contract without updating every production caller, test caller, and fixture that violates the new invariant.
modes.canonical_mitigation: For every input-contract change, generate a repository-wide inventory of direct and indirect call sites and fixtures, check each concrete argument or fixture against the new invariant, update every violation, and run all affected suites before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing a bug fix without a red-green reproduction
modes.definition: The agent changes production behavior or claims a bug fixed without first demonstrating the reported defect in a regression test and then showing that same test pass.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Block production edits until an issue-specific regression using the reported artifact and execution path has failed on the original behavior, then require that same test and the relevant regression suite to pass before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Requesting unnecessary clarification instead of answering
modes.definition: The agent withholds a sufficiently specified plan, recommendation, or set of options and asks for nonblocking clarification instead.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before asking a clarification question, run a sufficiency check over the stated goal, scope, and constraints; when a useful answer can be produced, require the requested plan, recommendation, or options to be delivered with explicit assumptions and reserve questions for ambiguities that make such an answer impossible.

modes.canonical_name: Hard-coding an environment-configured endpoint
modes.definition: The agent uses a literal service endpoint or fallback where requests are required to derive their endpoint from runtime configuration.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Route every request through one URL constructor that requires the designated environment setting, enforce configuration-precedence tests, and reject literal service hosts in request commands or default paths.

modes.canonical_name: Losing in-flight state across context switches
modes.definition: The agent associates an in-flight operation with mutable active-view state, causing updates to be finalized, discarded, or misrouted when the user switches contexts.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create an immutable state entry keyed by the originating context when each operation starts, route every callback through that key, and test rapid switching among concurrently active contexts for continuous updates and completion.

modes.canonical_name: Violating an established protocol flow
modes.definition: The agent proposes or implements direct, parallel, or relocated protocol behavior that contradicts an explicitly required synchronization and authorization sequence.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Maintain an approved invariant ledger and sequence diagram, then run an architectural acceptance test that disables bypass paths and verifies each required protocol step in order; reject any extra path or responsibility placement not explicitly approved.

modes.canonical_name: Launching a reproduction without reference parity
modes.definition: The agent launches an expensive reproduction while preprocessing, tokenization, optimization, batching, or context settings remain unverified against the reference.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Block launch until an automated parity gate compares every effective critical setting with reference code and documentation and passes golden tokenization and representative preprocessing checks, with every mismatch resolved or explicitly approved.

modes.canonical_name: Presenting uncorroborated conclusions as confirmed findings
modes.definition: The agent states a diagnosis, research conclusion, or absent control as confirmed without direct evidence from the relevant current-state enforcement point.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require every categorical finding to cite a current-state source inspection, configuration inspection, endpoint test, repeated trace, or authoritative document that directly supports it; otherwise force the finding to be labeled inferred, unverified, or hypothetical.

modes.canonical_name: Weakening test semantics to accommodate defective behavior
modes.definition: The agent changes valid fixtures, scenarios, or assertions so a defective implementation passes instead of correcting the exercised behavior.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before accepting a change to a failing test's setup, scenario, or assertion, require evidence that the existing expectation conflicts with the specification; absent that evidence, preserve the behavioral scenario and patch the implementation until the original regression passes.

modes.canonical_name: Asserting capability absence from unverified or stale sources
modes.definition: The agent claims a capability is absent without inspecting the authoritative source and exact active version or revision that determines its availability.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before an absence claim, verify the exact installed or pinned version, synchronize and inspect its source, schema, documentation, build configuration, and tests, then run a minimal capability probe and cite the resulting evidence.

modes.canonical_name: Verifying behavior through a path that bypasses production
modes.definition: The agent presents a harness or end-to-end test as verifying production behavior even though it reimplements, internally injects, or mocks the behavior instead of traversing the production interface.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require each verification artifact to identify the behavior under test and prove that execution reaches its exact production function, public transport, or real endpoint; reject local reimplementations, incompatible internal hooks, and mocks of that target behavior.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting required response fields
modes.definition: The agent delivers a response or report that omits one or more explicitly required fields, sections, or user-visible content elements.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Extract every required response field and section into an output schema, validate the final response against that schema before sending it, and block delivery when any required element is absent or empty.

modes.canonical_name: Marking feedback resolved without applying it
modes.definition: The agent identifies or acknowledges actionable feedback but reports it resolved without incorporating the corresponding change into the reviewed artifact.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Maintain a ledger mapping each actionable finding or revision request to a concrete artifact location and required change, and permit resolution only after a current diff and reread of that location verify the change was applied.

modes.canonical_name: Declaring review feedback absent from incomplete data
modes.definition: The agent concludes that no new or actionable review feedback exists after inspecting stale, partial, or non-paginated review data.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before concluding that review feedback is absent or complete, retrieve every review surface and page, including submissions, bodies, inline comments, thread replies, and top-level comments, then compare the newest IDs and timestamps against the feedback already processed.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving addressed review threads unresolved
modes.definition: The agent applies or discusses requested review changes but fails to perform and verify the separate action that marks the associated conversations resolved.
modes.canonical_mitigation: After applying each review fix, enumerate the targeted open thread IDs, invoke the thread-resolution operation for each one, and re-query them to verify every targeted thread reports a resolved state before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Planning instead of starting requested implementation
modes.definition: The agent continues planning, research, or confirmation-seeking after receiving a clear instruction to begin a non-destructive implementation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: On a clear implementation instruction, activate an execution mode that allows only minimal convention inspection, requires the first relevant edit within a fixed short budget, and permits further confirmation only for a material ambiguity, risky operation, or concrete blocker.

modes.canonical_name: Failing to continue asynchronous orchestration
modes.definition: The agent leaves an asynchronous or delegated workflow unfinished by failing to consume completed results, wait for all required terminal states, or synthesize the promised output.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Track every background or delegated task in a persistent orchestration state machine, automatically consume each completion result, continue its dependent steps, and block cleanup or completion until all required tasks are terminal and their outputs have been synthesized into the promised user-facing deliverable.

modes.canonical_name: Deleting requested or existing content without authorization
modes.definition: The agent deletes content without an explicit user instruction or confirmation authorizing removal of that specific content.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before every deletion, require a recorded user instruction or affirmative confirmation naming the exact content to remove; otherwise block the deletion, preserve the content, and request clarification.

modes.canonical_name: Creating or reporting an artifact at the wrong path
modes.definition: The agent creates, recommends, or reports an artifact at a path different from the exact path required or claimed.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Normalize the required and reported paths, capture the actual output path from the successful write or command, and reject completion unless all paths are equal and the artifact exists there.

modes.canonical_name: Committing directly on a branch requiring review isolation
modes.definition: The agent commits or pushes work on the default branch despite a requirement to use a separate feature branch and review workflow.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before staging or committing, compare the current branch with the protected or default branch list and require creation and checkout of a feature branch whenever isolated review was requested; enforce branch protection to reject direct pushes.

modes.canonical_name: Including unrelated paths in a scoped change set
modes.definition: The agent commits or publishes files outside the explicitly intended scope of the current task or reconstructed change set.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Construct an explicit task-owned path allowlist from the request and any authoritative prior change list, compare the staged or base-relative changed paths against it before checkpoint, commit, or push, and block on every unexpected path pending approval.

modes.canonical_name: Publishing unreconciled evaluation accounting
modes.definition: The agent reports benchmark results whose task membership, shard provenance, denominators, or subtotals do not reconcile with the underlying artifacts.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Generate reports from one task-ID manifest joined to raw results, and block publication unless a validator finds the expected unique tasks, correct shard membership, complete artifacts, and shard totals equal to the aggregate.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving deprecated dependencies after removal
modes.definition: The agent declares a dependency or concept removed while non-migration code still references its old package, type, field, claim, or parameter.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Maintain a repository-wide forbidden-reference list for every removed symbol and package, block completion while any non-migration match remains, and for package migrations also require a clean install and production build.

modes.canonical_name: Reading mutated data through a stale cache
modes.definition: The agent mutates underlying membership or object data but immediately reads through a cache that still represents the pre-mutation state.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require every relevant mutation or external fetch to invalidate or recreate the affected cached reader before returning, and test an initialized cache followed by mutation and immediate successful read.

modes.canonical_name: Changing a shared schema without updating consumers
modes.definition: The agent changes a shared payload or configuration structure while producers or runtime consumers still use the old contract.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Define the schema once in a shared typed contract, inventory and update every producer and property access atomically, and run an end-to-end test through serialization, transport, and rendering.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing consumers for unavailable upstream data
modes.definition: The agent builds downstream handling around event types, identifiers, or payloads that the relevant upstream producer does not emit.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Capture a representative runtime event trace for every producer and require a fixture proving the needed event type, parent identifiers, and payload fields exist before implementing the consumer; otherwise retain a supported path.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting an explicitly requested regression test
modes.definition: The agent completes an implementation without adding the automated regression test explicitly requested for the changed behavior.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Add a completion gate that maps each requested test scenario to a new or updated test case, verifies the case appears in the diff, and requires its targeted test command to pass.

modes.canonical_name: Failing to preserve explicitly required implementation
modes.definition: The agent removes or fails to relocate existing implementation that the plan explicitly requires to remain available.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Convert every named implementation-preservation requirement into a symbol-and-location checklist, inspect the final diff for each required implementation or approved equivalent, and compile and run a targeted test against the preserved code.

modes.canonical_name: Claiming a fix before updating the running artifact
modes.definition: The agent reports a source-level fix as available while the running system still uses an older built or deployed artifact.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before announcing remediation, rebuild the executable artifact, replace or restart stale instances, verify the running version or start time, and execute the targeted reproduction against the updated runtime.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing repeated fixes for unvalidated hypotheses
modes.definition: The agent repeatedly changes code and claims success without a controlled test that distinguishes the proposed cause from alternatives.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before each code change, record the hypothesis and predicted diagnostic signal, reproduce the exact failing stage, run a controlled isolation test or targeted instrumentation, and allow implementation only when the observed signal confirms the prediction.

modes.canonical_name: Declaring a CI-specific failure fixed from local results
modes.definition: The agent claims a CI-specific or instrumentation-dependent failure is fixed after testing only under local conditions that do not reproduce the failing workflow.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Reproduce the logged CI command, ordering, and instrumentation locally when possible and require a CI run containing the change with the original failure signature absent; otherwise label the change unverified.

modes.canonical_name: Submitting a CI fix before accounting for all failures
modes.definition: The agent reports or submits a CI remediation without inspecting and resolving or explicitly blocking every failed job in the relevant run.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Enumerate every failed job and failing step from the latest run, track each in a platform-by-platform checklist to an evidence-backed fix or validated external blocker, and require a clean targeted or full rerun before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Validating clean-environment behavior with persistent local state
modes.definition: The agent treats a stateful local run as equivalent to a fresh environment, allowing generated or installed artifacts to conceal first-run failures.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run the exact CI command with an isolated temporary home and data, config, and cache directories or after deleting the complete relevant installation and generated-artifact trees, then verify both first-run and idempotent behavior.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing instead of answering an advisory request
modes.definition: The agent begins investigation or modification work instead of first answering the user's requested feasibility, design, or architectural question.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Classify each request as advisory or implementation-oriented before using tools; for advisory requests, require a direct assessment with key tradeoffs before permitting repository edits or extended investigation, and require explicit implementation intent before modifications begin.

modes.canonical_name: Contradicting recorded user requirements
modes.definition: The agent plans or implements behavior that contradicts the user's recorded semantics, explicit choices, or rejected changes.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Maintain a decision ledger containing each stated behavior, confirmed choice, and explicit non-goal, then run a contradiction check against every proposed plan item and implementation mapping; block conflicting work and ask a targeted question when a term remains genuinely ambiguous.

modes.canonical_name: Producing deliverables without required source grounding
modes.definition: The agent produces a design or content artifact without reading and incorporating all source material the user explicitly required.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Enumerate the required source set into a manifest, record evidence that every relevant source was read, map each required deliverable section or claim to entries from that manifest, and block drafting or completion while any required source lacks coverage.

modes.canonical_name: Exhausting context without recoverable task state
modes.definition: The agent reaches the context limit without preserving sufficient task state to continue and verify the pending work.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Monitor remaining context capacity and, before the limit is reached, write a bounded external handoff containing completed work, unresolved requirements, validation status, repository state, and the exact next action, then resume in a fresh context from that handoff.

modes.canonical_name: Failing to initiate actionable error diagnosis
modes.definition: The agent responds generically or asks an open-ended question instead of beginning diagnosis from a sufficiently concrete user-reported failure.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Parse reported failures into command context, observed error, expected behavior, and available evidence; when these fields support any concrete diagnostic step, require that step to run before a response, and allow only targeted questions for missing information that blocks all diagnosis.

modes.canonical_name: Working toward the wrong objective
modes.definition: The agent performs or completes work whose objective and deliverables do not match the active user request.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Store the active requested outcome, decision criteria, and expected deliverable paths, then compare them with every proposed write and completion response; block actions that do not map to the stored objective and require task context to be re-established.

modes.canonical_name: Editing before required user decisions
modes.definition: The agent writes or commits an artifact before presenting required alternatives or obtaining and confirming the user's required decisions.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Represent every required choice as an unresolved decision state, prohibit writes and commits while any such state is unresolved, present the required alternatives or questions, and unlock editing only after the user's selection or confirmation is recorded.

modes.canonical_name: Bypassing mandatory workflow stages
modes.definition: The agent performs or reports work without completing all stages of an explicitly mandated workflow.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Instantiate the invoked workflow as an ordered checklist of required stages and completion artifacts, block implementation or publication until every artifact is recorded, and permit omission only when the user explicitly waives the named stage.

modes.canonical_name: Modifying existing artifacts under a create-only constraint
modes.definition: The agent changes pre-existing or unapproved artifacts when the task permits only creation of specified new artifacts.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Capture the initial artifact and version-control state, permit writes only to an explicit list of paths that were absent initially, and reject or revert every other change before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving superseded definitions after removal
modes.definition: The agent retains an implementation or public symbol that an approved consolidation or reduction explicitly requires removing.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Record every source path and symbol required to disappear, run repository-wide path and symbol searches before completion, and reject the change unless those definitions are absent and the diff contains the expected deletions or renames.

modes.canonical_name: Deleting unrelated behavior during feature removal
modes.definition: The agent removes independently useful behavior or coverage while deleting a specifically deprecated mechanism.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Build a deletion inventory mapping every removed implementation, command, caller, and test to the deprecated behavior, require replacement coverage where retained behavior moves, and block any unmapped deletion without explicit approval.

modes.canonical_name: Refusing simple reversible file creation
modes.definition: The agent repeatedly asks for optional details instead of performing an explicit, low-risk file-creation request.
modes.canonical_mitigation: When a filename is specified and creation is reversible, create it in the current project location with empty or minimally valid content, report the assumption and path, and ask first only if ambiguity would make the action unsafe or irreversible.

modes.canonical_name: Reviewing only part of the requested change set
modes.definition: The agent issues a whole-change review verdict without examining every staged, unstaged, and untracked artifact in scope.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Generate a manifest from staged, unstaged, and untracked change discovery, record a full read for every listed path, and block the final review verdict until each entry is covered or explicitly reported as inaccessible or excluded with justification.

modes.canonical_name: Skipping explicitly required validation before publication
modes.definition: The agent commits or publishes changes without successfully running every validation command explicitly required by the user.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Record each user-required validation command, execute it without narrowing or substitution against the final change set, and block commit or push until every command passes or the user explicitly accepts a reported blocker or failure.

modes.canonical_name: Mutating an issue without required checkout
modes.definition: The agent performs task work or changes issue state without first completing the required run-scoped checkout operation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Gate all task and issue mutations on a run-local record proving that the required checkout request succeeded for that issue during the current run.

modes.canonical_name: Assessing integration against a stale base
modes.definition: The agent creates or assesses a branch without first testing it against the current authoritative remote base.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Fetch the target base from the remote immediately before branch publication or mergeability assessment, perform a non-destructive trial merge or equivalent integration check against the fetched ref, and proceed only if it succeeds.

modes.canonical_name: Excluding changes from a commit-all request
modes.definition: The agent omits changed files despite an explicit instruction to commit all repository changes.
modes.canonical_mitigation: After a commit-all instruction, enumerate tracked, untracked, staged, and unstaged changes, stage all of them, and block the commit unless no changes remain or the user approves a documented exclusion list.

modes.canonical_name: Mutating repository state from the wrong worktree
modes.definition: The agent performs repository mutations from a worktree or branch other than the one designated for the operation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before each mutation, resolve the expected branch to its worktree, compare the current repository root and branch with the expected values, and execute the command through the verified absolute repository path only if both match.

modes.canonical_name: Discarding required changes through wholesale conflict resolution
modes.definition: The agent resolves a conflict by taking one side wholesale, thereby dropping required changes from the other side.
modes.canonical_mitigation: For every conflicted source file, compare base, ours, and theirs, prohibit whole-file side selection, verify that target-only and source-only required changes are represented in the resolution, and run the complete validation suite afterward.

modes.canonical_name: Using an unsupported command interface
modes.definition: The agent recommends or executes a command form that the installed executable does not expose or support.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inspect the installed executable's relevant help or command registration before use and require an argument-construction test confirming that the command and every supplied flag or positional argument match the exposed interface.

modes.canonical_name: Using invalid secret contexts in workflow conditions
modes.definition: The agent places secret references in workflow conditional contexts rejected by static workflow validation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run an Actions-aware validator after each workflow edit, map optional secrets into job or step environment variables, and condition on those variables rather than directly on the secret context.

modes.canonical_name: Delegating executable work unnecessarily
modes.definition: The agent gives the user operational instructions instead of performing an actionable task it can execute.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before delegating operational steps, check available tool and environment access, execute all noninteractive actions directly, and delegate only after recording a concrete credential, permission, payment, or interaction barrier.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving required features unwired at runtime
modes.definition: The agent implements a required component but fails to inject, register, or invoke it through the production execution path.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace each required feature from production construction through registration and invocation, enforce required dependencies as non-optional construction invariants, and require an end-to-end test through the real production factory.

modes.canonical_name: Skipping mandatory behavior on alternate paths
modes.definition: The agent keeps an accepted execution path on which a newly mandatory operation is omitted.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create a decision table for every accepted execution path and test that each path performs the mandatory operation exactly once or is rejected before processing; update parsers and builders for every preserved path.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving unattended commands interactive
modes.definition: The agent launches an unattended command that still requires an interactive confirmation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run the exact revised command in a clean foreground environment, require zero exit with no prompts using supported noninteractive options or initialization, and only then launch it unattended or update callers.

modes.canonical_name: Mutating deployed environments outside the required pipeline
modes.definition: The agent directly changes deployed systems despite a requirement that environment changes flow through version control, CI, or the configured secret manager.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Block SSH writes, direct container mutations, direct production database changes, and local environment-file edits; permit deployment changes only through committed configuration or migrations, approved secret APIs, verified CI runs, and designated promotion commands.

modes.canonical_name: Claiming runtime activation without artifact confirmation
modes.definition: The agent claims runtime remediation is active without confirming that the real runtime has loaded the newly built or modified artifact.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Resolve the artifact path used by the actual runtime, compare its version or build hash with the newly produced artifact, deploy it if necessary, restart the affected process, and require a successful post-restart health or acceptance check before claiming activation.

modes.canonical_name: Using minimum sizing when invariant sizing is required
modes.definition: The agent uses minimum dimensions for elements that must remain exactly equal in size across content or presentation variants.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Reject minimum-size-only rules for invariant-sizing requirements, require fixed dimensions or a shared stretch constraint, and compare computed inline and block dimensions across every supported variant and locale.

modes.canonical_name: Applying row styling only to content width
modes.definition: The agent applies a row-level background or selection treatment only across rendered content instead of the full required row width.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Size or pad each styled row to the container's target width and run a rendered-output snapshot that verifies every line contains the expected background cells through the full width, including borders and padding.

modes.canonical_name: Applying a global effect to a targeted consumer
modes.definition: The agent applies a refresh or event globally when only explicitly identified consumers should be affected.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require an affected-consumer manifest and a negative integration test proving that consumers outside the target set receive no event or refresh.

modes.canonical_name: Discarding session state after a partial commit
modes.definition: The agent deletes shared session state after one commit even though later commits from the same editing session still require checkpoints and metadata.
modes.canonical_mitigation: After each commit, recreate session storage at the new HEAD with all uncommitted touched files and carried metadata; test a multi-commit session for distinct, complete checkpoints.

modes.canonical_name: Registering an integration without capturing its session
modes.definition: The agent recognizes a new integration but fails to discover, parse, and preserve its session content.
modes.canonical_mitigation: For every registered integration, run a representative session through the commit workflow and assert that the resulting checkpoint contains nonempty session context from that integration.

modes.canonical_name: Breaking write authorization during receive-policy refactoring
modes.definition: The agent changes receive-side authorization and unintentionally rejects valid writes by authorized non-owners.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inventory read and write authorization call paths before changing permit state, then test that an authorized non-owner write is accepted and relayed end to end.

modes.canonical_name: Eagerly loading heavy children in list responses
modes.definition: The agent fetches large child collections for every parent in a paginated list, leaving list latency and payload size uncontrolled.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Enforce a list/detail split in which list responses contain only bounded metadata and children require explicit expansion; cap list query count, payload size, and latency in a performance test.

modes.canonical_name: Retrieving cached data without exact entity scope
modes.definition: The agent associates cached or persisted context with an entity using heuristic similarity instead of an exact durable identifier.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Store a dedicated indexed entity identifier on every record, require it on writes and reads, enforce exact equality in retrieval, and test isolation between similar and alphabetic-only identifiers.

modes.canonical_name: Assigning ownership without granting owner visibility
modes.definition: The agent makes ownership assignable without updating retrieval and authorization paths to expose the asset to the assigned owner.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace ownership from assignment through every access resolver and query, then test that the newly assigned owner can list and retrieve the asset.

modes.canonical_name: Compensating downstream for an invalid identifier
modes.definition: The agent changes downstream persistence to tolerate an identifier that violates the caller-facing identifier contract.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace the identifier from the input boundary to storage, declare its required type, and normalize or reject it at that boundary so downstream code receives only the contracted identifier.

modes.canonical_name: Coordinating restoration through fragmented state
modes.definition: The agent uses competing effects and persistent flags for one-shot restoration, allowing stale intents or saves to overwrite the intended position.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Implement restoration as one explicit phased state machine, atomically consume navigation intents, suppress saves until restoration completes, and test refresh, reverse navigation, and later layout changes.

modes.canonical_name: Dropping variants during content round trips
modes.definition: The agent persists or reconstructs composite content while silently losing required segment variants or order.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run round-trip tests containing every supported segment and tool variant, asserting exact segment types, values, and order after persistence and reload.

modes.canonical_name: Aggregating before canonical entity resolution
modes.definition: The agent groups display rows without first resolving multiple representations of the same underlying entity to one identity.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Resolve canonical identity from normalized authoritative attributes with documented fallbacks before grouping, and test that alternate representations of one entity yield exactly one row.

modes.canonical_name: Modifying persistence during presentation work
modes.definition: The agent changes data-writing or synchronization behavior while performing a presentation-only task, damaging existing persisted records.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Gate modifications to write-capable paths behind explicit approval for presentation-scoped tasks, and require a non-destructive merge invariant for any approved persistence change.

modes.canonical_name: Suppressing fallback output when primary state exists
modes.definition: The agent hides valid fallback output merely because primary execution metadata exists, even when the primary path failed.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Merge outputs from all sources by execution identifier rather than selecting by metadata presence, and test a failed primary path with visible fallback output.

modes.canonical_name: Resolving an artifact outside provider scope
modes.definition: The agent selects an artifact belonging to a different provider than the provider explicitly targeted by the request.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Restrict resolution to storage owned by the selected provider and test with colliding artifacts from multiple providers present.

modes.canonical_name: Passing a token to an incompatible verifier
modes.definition: The agent sends a session token to a verifier requiring a different issuer, signature algorithm, audience, or claims contract.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Obtain the exact runtime token in a contract test and pass it through the target verifier while asserting issuer, audience, algorithm, and required claims.

modes.canonical_name: Documenting behavior without tracing strategy differences
modes.definition: The agent documents strategy-specific behavior without verifying how each implementation path writes and reads the relevant artifacts.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Build a strategy-by-artifact matrix from concrete write and read call sites, and require every documentation claim and lookup direction to cite a matching implementation location or test.

modes.canonical_name: Adding logging metadata without call-site propagation
modes.definition: The agent adds metadata-capable logging APIs but does not pass the available value through runtime call sites.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace where the value becomes available, propagate it into every relevant logging context, and test a real runtime path for the emitted field.

modes.canonical_name: Exposing an untyped identity value as email
modes.definition: The agent presents a generic authentication identifier as an email despite records containing non-email subject identifiers.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Source email only from a semantically typed verified-email field, reject or migrate invalid legacy values, and prohibit fallback from email to generic subject IDs.

modes.canonical_name: Changing shared configuration without dependency alignment
modes.definition: The agent changes a shared configuration value without updating all components, scripts, clients, and documentation that depend on it.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Centralize the setting, inventory every default, environment variable, URL, startup script, and document that references it, update all dependencies, and run an end-to-end connectivity check.

modes.canonical_name: Delivering work outside the active session
modes.definition: The agent consumes or applies asynchronous work in a detached session while an existing interactive session is required to receive it visibly.
modes.canonical_mitigation: While any interactive session is live, retain the pending artifact and inject it into that session on its next prompt; permit detached application only after all sessions end, verified by a routing integration test.

modes.canonical_name: Reporting an identity inconsistent with runtime metadata
modes.definition: The agent reports a model identity that conflicts with trusted metadata for the running session.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Generate identity responses from trusted runtime model metadata through an exact identifier-to-public-name mapping, with no hardcoded fallback identity.

modes.canonical_name: Moving authorization redirects to client effects
modes.definition: The agent replaces server-controlled route protection with hydration-dependent client-side redirects.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Enforce server-side route authorization using the framework's documented request, data-access, or page-level checks, and reject authentication redirects implemented solely in client effects.

modes.canonical_name: Claiming source research without source access
modes.definition: The agent presents recommendations as derived from requested external sources without successfully accessing those sources.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Record a successful visit for every required source, attach source-specific observations to each recommendation, and label material lacking that provenance as prior knowledge or hypothesis.

modes.canonical_name: Silently retaining a deprecated storage fallback
modes.definition: The agent routes operations to a legacy backend when the required API backend is unavailable or unauthenticated.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Test every storage operation to ensure it either uses the required API or returns an explicit authentication error, and prohibit legacy reads or writes except inside an explicit migration procedure.

modes.canonical_name: Embedding producer conventions in a generic parser
modes.definition: The agent adds one producer's field conventions to parsing logic shared by distinct formats.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Dispatch through format-specific parser implementations and require separate fixtures proving that each parser accepts only its native fields and file conventions.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing live metrics with nonfunctional collectors
modes.definition: The agent presents required live metrics using mock, hardcoded, empty, or incorrectly decoded collector output.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run each collector on the target host, compare it with an authoritative system API or utility, reject constant or empty output, and verify the corresponding UI renders current nonempty data.

modes.canonical_name: Losing repository identity during data lookup
modes.definition: The agent resolves repository-owned resources through an implicit primary or incorrectly mapped database instead of the owning repository.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Carry a stable repository identifier through every link and request, resolve it through one canonical path-to-database mapping, and test resources from multiple configured repositories.

modes.canonical_name: Aggregating only the first capped result page
modes.definition: The agent computes a time-window aggregate from the first capped API page and omits additional records in the window.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Follow cursors until no results remain or the oldest result is outside the requested window, and test with records spanning multiple pages and buckets.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing an unconfirmed parameter interpretation
modes.definition: The agent repeatedly implements control semantics that do not match the requested geometric behavior.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Translate the request into explicit invariants and example values, compare them with existing controls, and require confirmation before editing whenever multiple interpretations satisfy the wording.

modes.canonical_name: Persisting through an unused identity path
modes.definition: The agent wires persistence to an identifier path not used by actual user-created console interactions.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace a UI-created console through creation and message delivery to its canonical identifier, centralize that mapping, and test that a UI-sent message persists under that exact ID.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting safeguards from an analogous workflow
modes.definition: The agent adds an analogous processing step without preserving the existing equivalent step's preconditions, output checks, and success gates.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require a structured parity matrix covering preconditions, directory creation, empty-output handling, error behavior, and downstream gates before accepting the new step.

modes.canonical_name: Reattaching from inside a nested multiplexer client
modes.definition: The agent detaches and attempts a fresh attachment from a process that remains inside the multiplexer environment.
modes.canonical_mitigation: When the multiplexer environment is set, map the invoking TTY to an attached client and switch that client; otherwise clear stale environment state and attach only from the outer terminal.

modes.canonical_name: Displaying results for a stale search query
modes.definition: The agent allows empty-input, old, or out-of-order search results to remain visible for the current query.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Clear results for empty input, issue searches for every supported nonempty input, and use cancellation or monotonic request IDs so only the latest response may update state.

modes.canonical_name: Inferring change provenance from file overlap
modes.definition: The agent attributes staged content to sessions by shared file paths rather than matching the sessions' actual changes.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Match checkpoint line patches or diffs against the staged diff, and test two sessions that modify different portions of the same file.

modes.canonical_name: Weakening required fields to fit invalid fixtures
modes.definition: The agent adds fallback behavior for data that the system contract requires, rather than rejecting invalid records and fixtures.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Express the field as required in storage constraints, types, and fixture builders, and test that missing values fail at the contract boundary instead of receiving a read-time fallback.

modes.canonical_name: Retrieving location context without spatial scope
modes.definition: The agent selects contextual notes globally or by recency instead of by proximity to the location in the current question.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Pass resolved coordinates or a bounding area into retrieval, filter stored notes by coordinates and radius, and test that distant notes are excluded.

modes.canonical_name: Breaking tree invariants in incremental updates
modes.definition: The agent replaces a canonical tree operation with an incremental implementation that mishandles structural path edge cases.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Differentially test canonical and incremental builders over generated changes plus file-directory transitions, deletion-only paths, nonexistent deletions, and platform-specific separators.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting required content from error logs
modes.definition: The agent adds an error warning but leaves out explicitly required raw content or identifying context.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Validate every relevant warning against a required-field checklist containing the error, identifying context, and raw content, with a log-capture test.

modes.canonical_name: Pre-classifying specialist input in the dispatcher
modes.definition: The agent lets a routing layer reinterpret or classify user content that the downstream specialist is responsible for deciding.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Limit dispatcher output to intent plus verbatim relevant excerpts, reject generated classifications or imperative rewrites, and test preservation of the user's original hierarchy.

modes.canonical_name: Producing a noncanonical artifact in an alternate workflow
modes.definition: The agent allows an alternate artifact-producing path to serialize producer-native data instead of the established normalized schema.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Route all workflows through the same normalization and serialization functions, then compare their metadata and message schemas for equivalent inputs.

modes.canonical_name: Debiting reimbursement from the wrong account
modes.definition: The agent pays a reimbursement from an account other than the one credited by fee collection.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace the fee-collection credit path before implementing payout, then test pre- and post-transfer balances for the actual credited account and recipient.

modes.canonical_name: Failing open on malformed enforcement input
modes.definition: The agent accepts structurally malformed or truncated enforcement input and compares partial observations as if setup succeeded.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Implement a validated parser state machine that rejects invalid field placement, empty reports, and open records at EOF before comparison; assert setup failure and no remediation output for each malformed fixture.

modes.canonical_name: Adding a retrieval limit from incorrect query semantics
modes.definition: The agent imposes a restrictive search heuristic after misattributing low recall to input size rather than query conjunction semantics.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Before adding a limit, run controlled single-predicate, conjunction, and disjunction experiments against documented semantics and compare recall with the previous behavior.

modes.canonical_name: Editing generated output outside its synchronization pipeline
modes.definition: The agent directly changes generated outputs instead of extending and running the designated source-to-output synchronization mechanism.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require template-to-output mappings in the tracked generation script, regenerate through that script, and verify that the resulting generated diff matches the requested change.

modes.canonical_name: Starting background work before client initialization
modes.definition: The agent starts background telemetry work before the client it depends on is fully configured.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Construct and configure the client synchronously before launching any dependent task, and repeatedly test startup for exported output without missing-client warnings.

modes.canonical_name: Mapping a role key to the wrong model family
modes.definition: The agent resolves a role-specific configuration key to a model family inconsistent with the role denoted by that key.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Compare every role-specific key with its resolved model identifier after generation and reject cross-family mappings unless explicitly allowlisted.

modes.canonical_name: Writing configuration with the wrong schema
modes.definition: The agent serializes integration settings using a key or identifier format the consuming application does not accept.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Derive the exact serialized shape from the authoritative schema, parser, or application-generated example and test that the real consumer accepts the resulting key and identifier.

modes.canonical_name: Referencing an identifier before allocation
modes.definition: The agent writes a guessed generated identifier into an artifact before the external system assigns the actual value.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create the external resource first, capture its returned identifier, and only then render or update every artifact that references it.

modes.canonical_name: Blocking startup during a concurrency refactor
modes.definition: The agent's worker or concurrency change prevents startup from returning and initializing the receive path.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run a timeout-bounded startup smoke test with the affected concurrency mode enabled, require the receive path to become operational, and capture thread or goroutine stacks on timeout.

modes.canonical_name: Routing unsupported input through a specialized extractor
modes.definition: The agent promotes a new input type into a pipeline whose extractor cannot represent that type's required output.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Dispatch explicitly by input type and require an end-to-end fixture proving that each supported type produces provenance consumed by downstream update and audit stages.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting known clients from an API consumer inventory
modes.definition: The agent recommends API evolution based on a consumer model that excludes applications or generated clients with direct dependencies.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Trace generated clients, package dependencies, and call sites into a repository-grounded consumer inventory and require explicit validation of that inventory before recommending versioning strategy.

modes.canonical_name: Changing a route prefix without updating clients
modes.definition: The agent moves server endpoints under a new prefix while built clients continue requesting the old paths.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Centralize the API prefix in shared configuration and run a built-application test that inspects browser request URLs and requires JSON responses from representative endpoints.

modes.canonical_name: Overwriting cumulative content instead of appending
modes.definition: The agent replaces a cumulative persistence file on each event, erasing prior entries.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Use one append helper with the defined delimiter and run a multi-event test asserting that every entry remains in order.

modes.canonical_name: Omitting acknowledgments from supported hook paths
modes.definition: The agent allows some successful lifecycle hooks to return without the required stdout acknowledgment.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Invoke every supported hook and repeated lifecycle path in a table-driven test and require each successful invocation to emit at least one stdout byte.

modes.canonical_name: Dropping a working index before validating its replacement
modes.definition: The agent removes an existing database index before proving that its replacement is valid and improves the target query.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create the replacement concurrently, verify readiness and validity, benchmark representative queries, and drop the old index only after all checks pass.

modes.canonical_name: Looking up relative paths from the wrong tree root
modes.definition: The agent performs relative metadata lookup against a tree whose root does not match the lookup's path convention.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Centralize selection of the canonical subtree and require all metadata reads to use paths relative to it; test the selected tree identity and lookup in a sharded checkpoint.

modes.canonical_name: Dismissing persistent failures as transient startup behavior
modes.definition: The agent labels repeated connection errors a harmless startup race without checking service and dependency health.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inspect service status and logs and probe the health endpoint before classifying errors as transient; allow that conclusion only if health recovers without intervention.

modes.canonical_name: Querying a field absent from the deployed schema
modes.definition: The agent issues a runtime query against a modeled field that is not present in the active database schema.
modes.canonical_mitigation: At change time, compare queried fields with the deployed migration state and block use of any column that is absent until its migration is available.

modes.canonical_name: Mutating data during read-only inspection
modes.definition: The agent opens inspected databases through write-capable access that modifies files or creates sidecars.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Open inspected databases with enforced read-only immutable settings and test snapshots of mtimes and directory contents to ensure no database, WAL, or SHM file changes.

modes.canonical_name: Adding a required field without updating constructors
modes.definition: The agent introduces a required model field but leaves one or more initializers unable to construct the model.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Search for every model initializer, update all construction sites, and compile every target and test suite before completion.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving downstream stages on the untransformed artifact
modes.definition: The agent creates a normalized artifact but downstream stages continue consuming the original source.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Replace the source reference with one canonical transformed-artifact path and run the complete pipeline, asserting normalized values in the final persisted output.

modes.canonical_name: Creating sharing grants without downstream access
modes.definition: The agent records resource sharing but downstream authorization does not recognize the recipient's grant.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Centralize effective access in a resolver that unions ownership, mappings, and active grants, require all services to use it, and test recipient access after creating a share.

modes.canonical_name: Generating component output incompatible with its schema
modes.definition: The agent supplies structured component instructions whose output cannot pass the renderer's parser and property schema.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Generate instructions from the authoritative component schema and pass every documented example through the same parser and property validator used by the UI.

modes.canonical_name: Reversing an explicitly required stack order
modes.definition: The agent renders stacked segments in the opposite order from the required smallest-to-largest arrangement around zero.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inspect built plot geometry and assert that the segment adjacent to zero on each side has the minimum value for its bar.

modes.canonical_name: Mapping multiple repositories to one database
modes.definition: The agent derives database paths from nonunique repository names or preserves legacy mappings that let distinct repositories share storage.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Derive paths from a stable unique repository identifier or canonical-path hash, detect duplicate and legacy shared mappings at startup, and migrate or reject them before serving.

modes.canonical_name: Masking backend failure as empty success
modes.definition: The agent converts a failed backend response into a successful empty value, concealing the underlying error.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require typed fetchers to throw on non-success responses, render an explicit error state, and verify the failing endpoint succeeds before closing the fix.

modes.canonical_name: Scanning full records for request-time aggregates
modes.definition: The agent implements a performance feature by fetching and processing large raw-record streams on every request.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require aggregate endpoints to use database aggregation, bounded sampling, or row limits and pass a representative viewport latency benchmark.

modes.canonical_name: Diagnosing repeated presentation as duplicate storage
modes.definition: The agent attributes a repeated UI item to duplicate database records without comparing entity identities and query sources.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Compare displayed entity IDs with underlying query results and distinguish one entity returned by multiple feeds from multiple stored entities before proposing deduplication.

modes.canonical_name: Substituting a conflicting persistence model
modes.definition: The agent stores data in a subsystem different from the explicitly required representation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Map every persistence requirement to concrete storage artifacts and acceptance tests, and block the change when the implementation uses a conflicting model.

modes.canonical_name: Inventing unsupported first-person evidence
modes.definition: The agent adds autobiographical details that the user did not provide or confirm in order to support a claim.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require a cited or user-provided source for every first-person fact; otherwise insert a TODO or request confirmation, and reject unsupported quantities, durations, and experiences.

modes.canonical_name: Introducing overlapping or cyclic service responsibilities
modes.definition: The agent adds abstractions that duplicate existing service ownership or create dependency cycles during architectural refactoring.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Require a reviewed responsibility matrix and dependency DAG for affected services, rejecting any duplicated operation ownership or cycle.

modes.canonical_name: Duplicating logic instead of delegating to the shared implementation
modes.definition: The agent copies existing behavior into a new handler despite an explicit requirement to reuse the shared implementation.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Expose the shared helper through an input-compatible interface and require the new handler to invoke it, with a call-level test proving delegation rather than copied behavior.

modes.canonical_name: Changing shared data for only one consumer
modes.definition: The agent changes a shared value to satisfy one consumer while violating other consumers' schema or rendering requirements.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inventory the shared field's schema and every consumer, choose or normalize to a representation accepted by all, and test each affected route and build step.

modes.canonical_name: Classifying all in-progress output as internal
modes.definition: The agent treats every pre-completion text segment as internal thinking, hiding legitimate streamed answers.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Classify using explicit block or segment metadata and test a mixed stream where internal orchestration remains hidden while answer text remains visible during streaming.

modes.canonical_name: Packaging unvalidated generated output
modes.definition: The agent packages generated output containing diagnostics or malformed content that is later executed as code or data.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Separate generated data from diagnostic stderr and parse or execute the exact artifact in a disposable environment before packaging it.

modes.canonical_name: Failing to persist updated concurrency state
modes.definition: The agent updates a concurrency token on some mutation paths but leaves other successful mutations using stale state.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Give every metadata-publishing mutation one shared result contract that requires persisting the returned sequence, and test consecutive create, rename, delete, and move operations.

modes.canonical_name: Assigning a field to the wrong domain entity
modes.definition: The agent places a field or relationship on an entity different from the one explicitly designated by the requirements.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Translate each ownership statement into an entity-field or relation-endpoint assertion and reject any schema change that violates those assertions.

modes.canonical_name: Stopping cleanup infrastructure before dependents
modes.definition: The agent shuts down a service needed for resource cleanup before cleanup-dependent components have released their resources.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Model shutdown dependencies explicitly, stop resource-owning dependents before their cleanup service, and test interrupt-driven shutdown for zero remaining managed resources.

modes.canonical_name: Leaving a required platform implementation behind
modes.definition: The agent completes a module extraction while a required platform-specific implementation remains in the legacy location or is absent from the target.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Compare every required source module with the target tree and verify that each feature-gated declaration resolves to an existing target implementation.

modes.canonical_name: Ignoring a corrected source-of-truth location
modes.definition: The agent continues designing lookups around superseded repositories after the user identifies the authoritative source location.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Record the corrected repository as an architecture constraint and validate every proposed lookup, cache, schema, and deployment step against that location.

modes.canonical_name: Rewriting explicitly preserved configuration structure
modes.definition: The agent consolidates or reorders configuration despite an explicit requirement to retain its original ordered structure.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Encode separate-entry and ordering invariants before editing and reject any diff that consolidates entries or reverses the required sequence.

modes.canonical_name: Handling in-band stream errors only as exceptions
modes.definition: The agent implements fallback only for thrown exceptions even though the stream can deliver failures as ordinary error-valued messages.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inspect every stream result before forwarding, route matching error values into the fallback path, and test a stream that yields an error result without throwing.

modes.canonical_name: Returning generic deduplication responses for endpoint-specific protocols
modes.definition: The agent reuses generic duplicate-request handling whose response violates the endpoint's externally visible protocol.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Send a duplicate request through the full verification and deduplication pipeline and assert the exact endpoint-specific status, content type, and body.

modes.canonical_name: Resolving future artifact paths from file existence alone
modes.definition: The agent cannot resolve an artifact's eventual path before the file exists even though surrounding layout signals determine it.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Specify path selection for each pre-creation layout state using parent directories and documented fallbacks, and test both existing-file and not-yet-created cases across supported layouts.

modes.canonical_name: Confusing backend reuse with pooled resource allocation
modes.definition: The agent treats caching an application backend as equivalent to allocating new claims from existing prewarmed infrastructure resources.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Record identities and creation times of prewarmed resources, create claims from distinct sessions, and assert that each claim binds an existing pool member rather than creating a new resource.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing the opposite cardinality constraint
modes.definition: The agent permits multiple entries when the requested behavior is to enforce at most one.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Confirm ambiguous cardinality wording before editing; when uniqueness is required, replace or reject an existing entry and test that exactly one remains.

modes.canonical_name: Skipping migration based only on target existence
modes.definition: The agent treats an existing target checkpoint as fully migrated even when a later source commit changed it.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Store the source commit with each migrated checkpoint and skip work only when the target records an exact commit match; test creation followed by an update in a later commit.

modes.canonical_name: Overwriting requested historical snapshots
modes.definition: The agent stores only the latest capture even though historical contents must remain available.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Write captures as timestamped or append-only snapshots keyed by stable source metadata and enforce an explicit retention or size policy.

modes.canonical_name: Inferring processing coverage from output presence
modes.definition: The agent treats output existence as proof of processing, making successful zero-result records indistinguishable from unprocessed records.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Persist explicit per-record processing state for each scope, including successful zero-result outcomes, and compute coverage only from that ledger with zero-result, uncovered, capped, and legacy tests.

modes.canonical_name: Cleaning stale resources in only one recovery path
modes.definition: The agent removes a stale resource in one deletion path while equivalent update or recovery paths can retain it and block reuse.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inventory every create, update, delete, and recovery path that can encounter the resource, apply one shared cleanup rule, and reproduce the upgrade scenario while asserting the original bind succeeds.

modes.canonical_name: Inferring an artifact path differently from the producing system
modes.definition: The agent asserts against an independently inferred artifact location that can disagree with the path actually selected and reported by the system under test.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Resolve the expected location from the same public inputs used by the producing command, compare it with the command-reported path, and assert that the exact reported artifact exists.

modes.canonical_name: Ignoring inherited values in effective configuration
modes.definition: The agent changes a local configuration source without inspecting higher- or lower-priority merged sources that keep the problematic value active.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Render or inspect the effective merged configuration from all application and dependency sources, identify the source of the active value, and require an explicit override in the highest-priority applicable source.

modes.canonical_name: Declaring production runtime behavior fixed after static checks
modes.definition: The agent declares a production-only browser behavior fixed using checks that do not execute the affected production-equivalent runtime path.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Load the affected pages in a production-equivalent browser build and assert the relevant scripts, placeholders, network requests, and callbacks execute successfully before permitting a fixed claim.

modes.canonical_name: Reporting absent coverage without measuring existing tests
modes.definition: The agent reports zero coverage without accounting for existing unit and integration tests that execute the target behavior.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run the repository's coverage tooling, map unit and integration tests to the target code paths, and require the coverage command and measured result in any zero-coverage finding.

modes.canonical_name: Regressing established calculations while extending scope
modes.definition: The agent extends a calculation for a new case while causing previously valid contributions or attributions to disappear or become incorrect.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Gate calculation-scope changes on the full tagged test suite plus invariant tests covering the new case and verifying that every previously supported contribution remains nonzero and correctly attributed.

modes.canonical_name: Substituting the wrong artifact for a requested benchmark workflow
modes.definition: The agent supplies an in-process test instead of the requested standalone executable benchmark workflow.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Reject completion unless an executable script exists and implements repository cloning, setup, control and enabled commits, separate timing output, and trap-based cleanup.

modes.canonical_name: Implementing only part of the requested fixture set
modes.definition: The agent supplies only a subset of explicitly requested static fixture categories needed to exercise distinct test paths.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Turn the requested fixture categories and minimum properties into a checklist, then verify each fixture is committed, satisfies its required size or format, and is referenced by the end-to-end helpers.

modes.canonical_name: Dismissing a discrepancy before tracing its execution path
modes.definition: The agent explains away a reported result before inspecting the exact job, command, dependency chain, and side effects that produced it.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inspect the exact job target and dependency graph, reproduce or trace every invoked command and side effect, and prohibit caching or stale-run explanations until that trace supports them.

modes.canonical_name: Assigning verification layers without a stable dependency model
modes.definition: The agent repeatedly changes verification-layer assignments without consistently applying a defined direct-call and stubbing rule.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Create a versioned table of each higher-level function, its direct callees, and which callees are stubbed, then mechanically derive and validate every verification-layer assignment from that table.

modes.canonical_name: Diagnosing skipped tests without enabling and running them
modes.definition: The agent confidently explains why tests are skipped without inspecting the skip conditions and executing the affected cases.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Inspect the skip annotations and corresponding implementation, temporarily enable the affected tests, run the targeted suite, and base any diagnosis on the observed result.

modes.canonical_name: Delegating requested UI verification to the user
modes.definition: The agent reports a UI change without reproducing and verifying the requested visual behavior in the running application.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Run the supplied reproduction in a browser, measure the relevant DOM dimensions or inspect overflow, and retain a screenshot or automated DOM assertion before reporting completion.

modes.canonical_name: Applying a dependency fix without validating reachability
modes.definition: The agent implements a hypothesized dependency remedy before proving that dependency reachability explains the observed request failure.
modes.canonical_mitigation: Reproduce the failing request, run bounded reachability checks for each required dependency from the same runtime environment, change only the dependency whose check fails, and rerun the full request.

modes.canonical_name: Resolving a test-relative path from the wrong directory
modes.definition: The agent constructs a test-relative path with the wrong parent traversal, preventing the intended artifact from being loaded.
